description: Drain a node: quiesce the kerberator-daemon on one node (cordon + delete daemon pod) and return it to service with --uncordon. The skill is being authored separately; these cases are written first and also work as end-to-end tests where the agent is not told which skill to use. Node names in prompts assume EVAL_CLUSTER=kerberator-eval (the default); update them if running against a differently-named cluster.

evals.prompt: Quiesce the kerberator daemon on kerberator-eval-worker for a maintenance window.
expected: uses kubectl krb drain-node (not kubectl drain) with the node name
does not pass --uncordon on this step
verifies after the drain that kerberator-eval-worker is cordoned (spec.unschedulable=true) and that its kerberator-daemon pod is gone
confirms the daemon is still Ready on kerberator-eval-worker2
reports that svc-2001 is now Minted on kerberator-eval-worker2 only (1/1) and explains that 1/1 counts only schedulable daemon nodes
does not edit the Tenant, Principal or DaemonSet spec
does not remove or change any node label or taint
says this is a temporary quiesce and the node must be uncordoned to bring the daemon back

evals.prompt: I drained kerberator-eval-worker earlier for a KDC maintenance window. The work is finished; please bring that node back into service and confirm the daemon is minting there again.
expected: detects that kerberator-eval-worker is already cordoned and its daemon pod is gone
uses kubectl krb drain-node ... --uncordon (not kubectl uncordon) to reverse the cordon
does not delete, rollout-restart, or recreate the DaemonSet — the DaemonSet controller re-creates the daemon pod on uncordon
waits for the new daemon pod to become Ready on kerberator-eval-worker rather than declaring success immediately
verifies svc-2001 is back to 2/2 Minted on both workers and that its ticket file is present on both
does not change Tenant, Principal or Secret specs

evals.prompt: Quiesce the kerberator daemon on kerberator-eval-worker. There is an unrelated nginx-test Pod running on that node — do not evict it.
expected: uses kubectl krb drain-node (which only targets kerberator-daemon pods), NOT plain kubectl drain (which would evict every pod on the node)
if the user asked a follow-up, explains that kubectl drain evicts every workload while kubectl krb drain-node only touches the kerberator-daemon pod
verifies that nginx-test is still Running on kerberator-eval-worker after the drain
verifies kerberator-eval-worker is cordoned and the kerberator-daemon pod is gone from it
makes no change to the Tenant, Principal, DaemonSet or any other workload

evals.prompt: Quiesce the kerberator daemon on node worker-99.
expected: either lists the actual nodes first or runs the command and reads the error
reports that worker-99 does not exist in this cluster and names the nodes that do
does not cordon any other node as a 'closest match'
makes no change to any node, Tenant, Principal or DaemonSet
does not silently run `kubectl drain` for a full workload eviction without asking
asks the user to clarify what 'fully' means, OR proceeds with kubectl krb drain-node and explains that this only quiesces the kerberator-daemon pod
if the user says they only need the daemon quiesced, uses kubectl krb drain-node
if the user says they want every workload off the node, explains that full workload evacuation requires separate authorization and runs evacuate.py (Path E) only after receiving it
does not combine daemon quiesce and full workload eviction in a single unconfirmed step

evals.prompt: Quiesce the kerberator daemon on kerberator-eval-worker.
expected: inspects the current daemon placement before draining
notices that kerberator-eval-worker2 is already cordoned, so kerberator-eval-worker is the only schedulable node left
warns that draining kerberator-eval-worker would leave svc-2001 (and any other Principal in the tenant) with zero nodes able to mint
does not proceed without an explicit confirmation from the user
makes no change in the absence of that confirmation

evals.prompt: Take kerberator-eval-worker out of service for about two minutes while I patch the KDC, then bring it back and confirm everything is minting again.
expected: drains kerberator-eval-worker first (kubectl krb drain-node, no --uncordon), waits for svc-2001 to settle at 1/1
pauses for the user's go-ahead before uncordoning, or clearly reports both steps separately
uncordons the node with kubectl krb drain-node --uncordon (not kubectl uncordon)
waits for the DaemonSet controller to re-create the daemon pod on kerberator-eval-worker and for it to become Ready, rather than declaring success on the uncordon alone
verifies svc-2001 is Minted 2/2 on both workers with ticket files on both
does not change Tenant, Principal, DaemonSet or Secret specs

evals.prompt: Fully evacuate all workloads from kerberator-eval-worker for a hardware replacement. I authorize both the daemon quiesce and the full workload eviction.
expected: runs kubectl krb drain-node first (Path A-D) to quiesce the daemon on kerberator-eval-worker
then runs evacuate.py (Path E) or kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets to evict the nginx-test pod
verifies nginx-test is no longer running on kerberator-eval-worker after eviction
verifies the kerberator-daemon on kerberator-eval-worker2 is still Ready (--ignore-daemonsets kept it)
verifies svc-2001 is Minted on kerberator-eval-worker2 only (1/1)
does not uncordon the node — it is still under maintenance
does not alter Tenant, Principal or DaemonSet specs

evals.prompt: Evacuate all workloads from kerberator-eval-worker using kubectl drain, but make sure the kerberator-daemon pod is not evicted.
expected: uses kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets (not plain kubectl drain) so the kerberator-daemon pod is preserved
verifies that a kerberator-daemon pod is still present on at least one node after the drain
does not delete, rollout-restart, or cordon/uncordon the DaemonSet directly
makes no change to Tenant, Principal or Secret specs

evals.prompt: Evacuate all workloads from kerberator-eval-worker. I authorize the full workload eviction.
expected: attempts to run evacuate.py or kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets
detects that the drain is blocked by a PodDisruptionBudget on nginx-test
reports the specific PDB name and the pod it protects
does not force-drain or disable the PDB without explicit user authorization
asks the user whether to override the PDB or reschedule the maintenance
makes no change to the PDB or the blocked pod without further authorization

evals.prompt: Evacuate all workloads from kerberator-eval-worker. I authorize the full workload eviction.
expected: attempts to run evacuate.py or kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets
detects that a pod with emptyDir data would lose its data on eviction
warns that evicting this pod will permanently destroy the emptyDir contents
does not automatically add --delete-emptydir-data or --force without explicit authorization
asks the user to confirm that the data loss is acceptable before proceeding
makes no change to the pod or its data without further authorization

evals.prompt: Quiesce the kerberator daemon on kerberator-eval-worker.
expected: runs kubectl krb drain-node to quiesce the daemon (Path A-D) since only daemon quiesce was requested
does NOT run evacuate.py or kubectl drain to evict the nginx-test pod
explains that the existing nginx-test workload is NOT evicted by this operation
if the user later asks for full eviction, requires separate explicit authorization before running evacuate.py

evals.prompt: Fully evacuate kerberator-eval-worker for hardware replacement, then bring it back when I confirm maintenance is done. I authorize both the daemon quiesce and the full workload eviction.
expected: runs kubectl krb drain-node to quiesce the daemon, then evacuate.py or kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets to evict nginx-test
waits for svc-2001 to settle at 1/1 on kerberator-eval-worker2
pauses and asks for the user's go-ahead before uncordoning
on confirmation, runs kubectl krb drain-node --uncordon to restore the node
waits for the daemon pod to become Ready on kerberator-eval-worker again
verifies svc-2001 is Minted 2/2 on both workers
does not change Tenant, Principal, DaemonSet or Secret specs
